findings.message: Criterion 2 is not tested. It requires a host serve whose engine checkout differs from the host repo to hand off at its next admission check after the engine's `chupa` tree changes outside serve. Both new handoff tests set `rig.owner.engine = root`, which makes the engine the host repo, and no test uses a separate engine checkout.
findings.paved_road: Add a test that sets `rig.owner.engine` to a separate git checkout under tmp_path with its own `chupa/` tree. Commit a `chupa/` change there while serve is idle and do not call `check_upgrade` by hand. Assert that serve journals `serve_handoff` and spawns once from its own admission-boundary check.

findings.message: Criterion 1 says a merge touching `chupa/` triggers the handoff, and the ticket requires the tree check at admission and merge-queue boundaries. Both tests commit straight to the repo and then call `rig.owner.check_upgrade()` directly. The calls in `respond`/`merge` (serve.py) are never exercised, so the tests would still pass if those boundary calls were removed. The docs-only case also never goes through a merge.
findings.paved_road: Drive the change through a real serve merge, as other serve tests do: a ticket whose implement step changes `chupa/` (or only `docs/`). Let serve's own post-merge and pre-admission `check_upgrade` calls detect it, without calling `check_upgrade` from the test.
